skill.name: fix-sentry-issues
skill.description: Discover, triage, reproduce, and fix Sentry issues through root-cause analysis. Uses Sentry MCP and optional Axiom context to investigate production failures.
skill.summary: Investigate Sentry events, identify root causes, and guide verified issue-specific fixes.
skill.author: brianlovin

security_audit.summary: Most backtick detections are Markdown code formatting, not Ruby or shell execution. The skill directs agents to run Axiom and Git commands and fetch production-derived URLs, creating command, network, and data-handling risks. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The Axiom command inserts a trace identifier into a shell command.
remediation.suggestion: Validate trace identifiers and invoke the CLI with structured arguments instead of shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: The workflow fetches URLs taken from production events.
remediation.suggestion: Require URL validation, block private network targets, and request confirmation before sending network requests.

remediation.issue: Actual Sentry inputs may enter tests without redaction.
remediation.suggestion: Remove secrets and personal data, then replace production values with minimal synthetic fixtures.

remediation.issue: The workflow runs Git commands that change branches and pull remote updates.
remediation.suggestion: Validate generated branch names and request confirmation before changing repository state or contacting remotes.

content.user_title: Fix Sentry Issues with Root-Cause Analysis
content.value_statement: Production error queues often hide the upstream defect behind repeated symptoms. This skill uses Sentry evidence and code tracing to guide focused, verified fixes.
actual_capabilities: Discovers Sentry organizations, projects, unresolved issues, and event details through Sentry MCP.
Classifies issues for investigation or dismissal using event volume, recurrence, and user impact.
Correlates Sentry events with Axiom logs by trace identifier when the Axiom CLI is available.
Traces failing inputs through application code to identify upstream root causes.
Creates one issue-specific branch and guides test-first fixes using representative event data.
Updates Sentry issue status after investigation or after a verified fix is merged.
limitations: Requires a configured Sentry MCP server and permission to read or update the selected project.
Axiom correlation assumes the Axiom CLI, authenticated access, and the named event dataset are available.
Production inputs may be unsafe to fetch or store, so users must validate URLs and redact sensitive data.
The skill cannot confirm production recovery before deployment and new Sentry events.

use_cases.title: Triage an Error Backlog
use_cases.description: Rank unresolved issues by recurrence and user impact, then identify items requiring investigation.

use_cases.title: Debug a Recurring Failure
use_cases.description: Trace event inputs, stack frames, and request context to find the upstream application defect.

use_cases.title: Prepare Focused Fixes
use_cases.description: Create issue-specific branches, regression tests, and pull request summaries with clear root-cause evidence.

prompt_templates.title: List Issues for Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: List unresolved Sentry issues for {project}. Build a triage table with issue ID, event count, action, and evidence. Do not change statuses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an unresolved issue queue

prompt_templates.title: Investigate One Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate Sentry issue {issue_id}. Retrieve event details, identify recurring inputs, follow the stack trace, and explain the likely root cause.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused investigation using Sentry event data

prompt_templates.title: Correlate Event Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Correlate Sentry issue {issue_id} with Axiom using its trace identifier. Redact sensitive values and summarize the surrounding request context.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Verified Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix Sentry issue {issue_id} in {repository}. Confirm the root cause first. Add a failing regression test, implement the smallest fix, and verify checks.

output_examples.input: Triage unresolved checkout issues without changing their status.
output: Investigate CHECKOUT-42: 118 events affect payment confirmation across three releases.
Ignore CHECKOUT-19: two browser-extension events contain no application stack frames.
Next step: inspect event inputs and stack traces for CHECKOUT-42.

output_examples.input: Investigate API-77 and explain the root cause.
output_examples.output: API-77 receives binary document URLs on a text extraction path. Input classification is missing before the external extraction request.

output_examples.input: Prepare a fix summary for a merged timeout issue.
output_examples.output: Root cause: oversized inputs reached a synchronous parser. Fix: reject unsupported sizes upstream and cover the production failure shape with a sanitized regression test.

best_practices: Investigate one issue at a time and preserve status codes, stack traces, and original error details.
Redact secrets and personal data before storing Sentry inputs in tests, logs, or pull requests.
Validate production-derived URLs before fetching them, and require confirmation for remote status changes.
anti_patterns: Do not classify recurring fallbacks as expected without tracing why the primary path failed.
Do not combine unrelated Sentry issues in one branch or pull request.
Do not resolve issues or lower log levels before verifying the root cause and deployed fix.

faq.question: Does this skill require Sentry MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Sentry MCP to discover projects, search issues, inspect events, and update issue status.

faq.question: Does it automatically resolve Sentry issues?
faq.answer: No. Resolution should occur only after the fix is merged and verified.

faq.question: Can it investigate several issues together?
faq.answer: It can triage a queue, but investigation and fixes should proceed one issue at a time.

faq.question: Is Axiom required?
faq.answer: No. Axiom provides optional trace context when its CLI, dataset, and credentials are available.

faq.question: How should production event data be handled?
faq.answer: Redact secrets and personal data, minimize retained fields, and use synthetic fixtures when possible.

faq.question: What should a completed fix include?
faq.answer: Include root-cause evidence, a regression test, the focused code change, passing checks, and a clear pull request summary.
